issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires Farm to initialize its internal ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments, but the solution implementation only provides a constructor Farm(int initialCapacity) and lacks a no-argument constructor. This constructor-parameter mismatch can confuse students about which constructor to implement and may cause tests or examples that expect a no-arg Farm() to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument constructor in Farm that initializes animals = new ArrayList<>(), or include an additional no-arg constructor alongside the existing Farm(int) constructor so the implementation matches the problem specification. Update solution and/or template so the expected Farm() constructor exists.
